cases.rationale: POST /reports has neither operationId nor summary/description; the rule must fire for both missing requirements simultaneously.
GET /status has both operationId and description; the rule must not fire.
GET /records has operationId but neither summary nor description; rule fires for the summary-or-description requirement only.
GET /exports has a description but no operationId; rule fires for operationId only.
GET /notifications has operationId and a whitespace-only summary; after trim the summary is empty, so the rule fires. Boundary for trimming behaviour in OAS 3.1.x.
GET /categories has operationId and an empty-string description; empty string trims to empty, so the rule fires. Boundary for empty-string vs absent description.
POST /batches has neither operationId nor summary/description in OAS 3.1.x; rule fires for both requirements.
POST /jobs has operationId and a non-empty summary; summary alone satisfies the summary-or-description condition. Boundary: no description present.
GET /metrics has operationId and a non-empty description; description alone satisfies the summary-or-description condition in OAS 3.1.x.
GET /tags has a whitespace-only summary and a valid description; whitespace summary is discarded but the description satisfies the condition. Boundary for 'either passes' logic.
GET /version has operationId and a summary with surrounding whitespace; after trim the summary is non-empty and passes. Boundary complement to syn-ctx-whitespace-summary-31.
GET /items has a query parameter 'page' without description; the rule must emit one finding for the missing description.
GET /catalog has only an Authorization header parameter, which is explicitly excluded from AGT-PARAM-001 by the rule spec; no finding expected.
GET /users/{userId} has a required path parameter 'userId' with no description; the rule fires for path parameters lacking description.
GET /sessions/current has a cookie parameter 'sessionId' with no description; covers the in:cookie dimension.
GET /events has a custom header X-Trace-Id with no description; custom headers are not excluded, so the rule fires in OAS 3.1.x.
GET /downloads has only an Accept header parameter without description; Accept is excluded by the rule spec.
GET /products has two query params; 'page' has a description but 'limit' does not. Only the non-compliant param generates a finding.
GET /reports has three query parameters (from, to, status) all without descriptions; the rule emits one finding per parameter, producing three findings.
POST /uploads has only a Content-Type header parameter without description; Content-Type is excluded by the rule spec.
GET /devices has three query parameters all with descriptions; no finding expected.
GET /organizations/{orgId} has a path parameter 'orgId' with a description; path parameters with descriptions pass the rule.
GET /preferences has an AUTHORIZATION header parameter (all caps) without description; case-insensitive exclusion means AUTHORIZATION is excluded same as Authorization.
DELETE /tasks/{taskId} has a valid confirmation policy but no 4xx/5xx/default response with a JSON schema; AGT-RESP-001 must fire. AGT-POL-001 is silent because confirmation.mode is required.
DELETE /sessions/{sessionId} has a default response with application/problem+json and a schema; AGT-RESP-001 must not fire. The boundary is the +json media-type suffix satisfying the rule condition.
DELETE /archive/{entryId} has only a method-category signal (no keyword or path risk tokens); no error response exists so RESP-001 fires.

POST /runs is applicable by condition 1 (state-changing method) with no risk tokens; no error response exists so RESP-001 fires. POST method evidence is emitted by the RESP rule, not a risk-classifier signal.
PUT /records/{recordId} is applicable by condition 1 with no risk tokens; no error response so RESP-001 fires.
PATCH /documents/{documentId} is applicable by condition 1 with no risk tokens; no error response so RESP-001 fires.
POST /payments has a 400 response but with text/plain content type; RESP-001 fires because no application/json or +json error response exists.
POST /subscriptions has a 400 response but with no content or schema; RESP-001 fires because a schema is required.
PUT /configs/{configId} has a 4XX wildcard response with application/json and a schema; RESP-001 must not fire.
POST /builds has a 5XX wildcard response with application/json and a schema; RESP-001 must not fire.
PATCH /settings/{settingId} has a concrete 400 response with application/json and a schema; RESP-001 must not fire.
GET /users/{userId}/credentials is classified as sensitive_data; GET with sensitive_data only does not satisfy either RESP-001 applicability condition.

GET /queue has x-agent-policy.risks:[destructive]; extension classifier assigns destructive satisfying RESP-001 condition 2. No error response exists so RESP-001 fires with the method signal and explicit-risk evidence.
POST /transfers is classified as financial_action via path token 'transfers' and operationId token 'transfer', but has no x-agent-policy.confirmation; AGT-POL-001 must fire.
POST /search has no risk-classified tokens; AGT-POL-001 must not fire even though POST is a state-changing method.
DELETE /cache is classified destructive by method-category alone; no x-agent-policy.confirmation exists so POL-001 fires at the Operation Object pointer.
POST /notifications classified as external_side_effect by path segment alone; no confirmation so POL-001 fires.
POST /permissions classified as permission_change by path segment; x-agent-policy present (authorization only) but confirmation key absent so POL-001 fires at Operation Object pointer.
POST /tasks/actions classified as destructive by operationId keyword 'cancel' alone; no confirmation so POL-001 fires.
GET /batch/status classified as external_side_effect by x-agent-policy.risks extension; x-agent-policy has no confirmation key so POL-001 fires at Operation Object pointer.

DELETE /payments/{paymentId} classified as destructive (DELETE method) and financial_action (keyword 'payment', path 'payment' from {paymentId}, path 'payments'); four evidence items; no confirmation so POL-001 fires.
POST /webhooks has confirmation mode:conditional with a non-empty condition string; POL-001 passes.
POST /invoices has confirmation mode:not-required with a non-empty reason string; POL-001 passes.
POST /grants has confirmation mode:conditional but the required 'condition' field is absent; schema-invalid confirmation fires POL-001 at the confirmation object pointer.
POST /purges has confirmation mode:not-required but the required 'reason' field is absent; schema-invalid confirmation fires POL-001 at the confirmation object pointer.
POST /charges has confirmation mode:required; required mode is unconditionally valid so POL-001 passes.
GET /transfers: 'transfer'/'transfers' are financial_action tokens but stateChangingTokenCategories require a state-changing method; GET does not qualify so no classification occurs.
GET /users/{userId}/secrets is classified as sensitive_data; the operation overrides global security with security: [], making effective security empty; AGT-POL-002 must fire.

PATCH /admin/roles is classified as permission_change with effective inherited security and x-agent-policy.authorization.roles declared; AGT-POL-002 must not fire. AGT-POL-001 is silent because confirmation.mode is required.
POST /roles classified as permission_change; security passes (global bearerAuth), but x-agent-policy has no authorization.roles; POL-002 fires at x-agent-policy pointer.
GET /profiles classified as sensitive_data; security passes but dataClassification:public is insufficient; POL-002 fires at dataClassification field pointer.
GET /credentials/{credentialId} has security:[{}] (anonymous override); anonymous security does not pass; POL-002 fires at op-level security field pointer.
GET /tokens classified as sensitive_data; security passes but x-agent-policy is absent; no present-but-inadequate policy field so POL-002 fires at Operation Object pointer.
POST /access/credentials has both risks; security and dataClassification:confidential pass but authorization.roles is absent; POL-002 fires at x-agent-policy pointer.
GET /credentials/{credentialId} in OAS 3.0.x: inherited global bearerAuth security passes; dataClassification:confidential passes; POL-002 must not fire.
GET /secrets/{secretId}: inherited global bearerAuth security passes; dataClassification:restricted passes; POL-002 must not fire.
PATCH /roles/{roleId}/secrets has both risks; all requirements met: global bearerAuth security, dataClassification:confidential, authorization.roles:[admin]; POL-002 must not fire.
GET /roles: 'roles' is a permission_change token but stateChangingTokenCategories requires a state-changing method; GET is excluded so no classification occurs.
